spots.name: Doughmore
spots.hazards: DANGEROUS RIP CURRENTS — strong rips pull out across this bay and are the main hazard; know your exits before paddling out. Exposed flat rocks at low tide on the reef side (left/north). Big open beach — conditions and currents vary along its length.
spots.notes: Large, open beach — effectively two spots. The main sandy beach (the usual surf) is a forgiving beach break, rights and lefts, working ALL tides. A separate powerful left-hand reef over flat rocks sits to the left/north: advanced only, needs 1.5 m+, best mid-high once the rocks are covered — it does NOT work all tides like the beach. Very consistent year-round; best Oct-Mar. Rarely crowded even when it's on.

spots.name: Spanish Point
spots.hazards: Submerged rocks near the point, especially at low tide; rips pull offshore on bigger swells.
spots.notes: Long sandy beach break near Miltown Malbay with a point at one end — mellow rights and lefts, waist-to-head-high, forgiving and approachable. Works all tides, though mid tide usually shapes the best peaks. Fairly consistent year-round; best Sep-Mar on W/SW swell, up to 2-3 m in autumn/winter. Great for beginners and for practising turns; the point comes alive on bigger SW swells. Usually empty midweek. Avoid prolonged S or W winds — they chop it up.

spots.name: Lahinch
spots.hazards: Rips on bigger swells; scattered rocks at the headland ends.
spots.notes: Classic sandy beach break in front of the village — rights and lefts, punchy A-frames on clean days, holds to ~2 m. Best on low-mid tide. Regular consistency, peaks Sep-Mar on NW/W groundswell; summer is smaller but fun. Suits everyone: beginners inside, bigger winter lines outside. Surf shops, rentals and cafes on the beach. Often crowded, but it's long enough to find your own peak.

spots.name: Fanore
spots.hazards: Rocks exposed at low tide; rips on bigger swells; jellyfish in summer (booties help).
spots.notes: Beginner-friendly beach break in the Burren — sand with some rock, rights and lefts, waist-to-head-high. Mid tide is the window. Decent consistency on NW swell, best Oct-Mar; can go flat midsummer. Usually empty midweek. Lifeguards in summer. Great for building confidence or a warm-up session.

spots.name: White Strand
spots.hazards: Rips and undertow, especially above 1.5 m; rocks exposed at low tide — part of why it needs high tide.
spots.notes: Sheltered beach break (aka Killard) near Doonbeg — mellow A-frames, rights and lefts, sand with rocky outcrops. HIGH tide only, and best on a RISING tide: that's what covers the rocks and makes the wave. Needs a decent swell (from ~2.5 m) to start working. Best Oct-Mar; flat most of summer. Almost always empty.

spots.name: Easkey Left
spots.hazards: Rocks in the take-off zone; rip off the pier on bigger swells. Boulder bottom — booties recommended.
spots.notes: Left-hand reef over boulders by the Easkey rivermouth — hollow, fast, barrels on the right swell. Works all tides; low tide sharpens the take-off over the rocks. Fairly consistent, best Dec-Feb on NW groundswell with a S offshore; often flat in summer. Fine for improvers on smaller days, proper reef wave when it's bigger. O'Dowd's Castle at the pier.

spots.name: Easkey Right
spots.hazards: Sharp reef and rocks — precision essential. Avoid above ~1.8 m unless very experienced. Rocks wash in on bigger swells, and the rivermouth rip pushes you off the peak.
spots.notes: Powerful right-hand POINT break over sharp reef — long walls, hollow when it's firing, one of Ireland's best. LOW tide only for clean shape. Park right in front. Use the rivermouth rip to get out. Remarkably consistent, best Nov-Mar. Intermediate-plus: you need solid board control for the reef.

spots.name: Strandhill
spots.hazards: Strong rips; rocks poke through at low tide or after winter erosion. High tide can cut off access near the promenade.
spots.notes: Very consistent beach/sandbar break under Knocknarea (~150 days a year) — rights and lefts off shifting banks, occasional hollow sections. Mid-high tide is prime; low gets shorey and rocky. Best when the swell stays under 2 m — big mid-winter swells close it out. Surf schools in the village, so good for progression. Low crowds on a wide beach.

spots.name: Bertra
spots.hazards: Currents in the channel between the spit and Clew Bay. The tide changes the beach shape — keep an eye on it. Busy with families in summer. Cold water: proper wetsuit outside high summer.
spots.notes: Long, narrow tombolo beach reaching into Clew Bay near Westport, under Croagh Patrick — some of the best scenery in the country. Forgiving, family-friendly and a local pick on smaller days. Partly sheltered by Clew Bay and Clare Island, so it picks up less swell than the open Atlantic beaches: that makes it the reliable fallback when the open coast is too big or messy. Faces W; works most tides with mid the sweet spot, on a WSW-NW swell (best period 10-16 s) with an E offshore. Best Sep-Apr, though summer works too.

spots.name: Keel
spots.hazards: Rips on bigger SW swells; exposed rocks at low tide.
spots.notes: Achill Island beach break over sand — lefts and rights, fun A-frames, waist-to-head-high. Needs SW swell (it won't work on the W/NW that suits the Clare/Sligo spots) with NE/E offshore. Mid-high tide when the sandbars peak. Fairly consistent, best Sep-Mar. Remote island setting; quiet midweek, busier weekends.

spots.name: The Magharees
spots.hazards: Rips form in bigger surf across the wide beach — paddle wide to escape. No significant rocks.
spots.notes: Brandon Bay / the Maharees on the Dingle Peninsula — an 11 km sandy beach with multiple peaks (Gowlane, Dumps, Mozzies), lefts and rights. Works ALL tides, which makes it very flexible. Mellow and forgiving, ideal for beginners and longboarding; fun shapes for everyone on bigger days. Rarely flat, best Sep-Apr. Almost always empty.
